title: K-injective derived direct-image comparisons for subterminal slices
statement:
Let $(\mathcal E,J)$ be a small subcanonical site with finite limits, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $U,V\hookrightarrow1$ subterminal objects; no covering hypothesis is imposed. Put $W=U\times V$. Use the module categories [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] on $\mathcal E$ and its localized ringed sites [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and their unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $j_Z^*$ for restriction to $Z=U,V,W$ and $k_U^*,k_V^*$ for restriction to $W$ within the $U,V$ slices. All these module categories admit K-injective resolutions [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Restriction and its underived right adjoint preserve K-injective complexes. On module sheaves this right adjoint is
$$(j_{Z*}F)(C)=F(C\times Z\to Z),$$
with $R(C)$ acting by restriction to $R(C\times Z)$; $k_{U*},k_{V*}$ have the same formula inside the slices. Thus $j_Z^*\dashv Rj_{Z*}$ on unbounded derived categories, and $Rj_{Z*}(Q I)=Q(j_{Z*}I)$ for every K-injective complex $I$ on the slice, where $Q$ denotes localization. There are natural derived identifications
$$j_U^*Rj_{U*}A\cong A,\quad j_U^*Rj_{V*}B\cong Rk_{U*}(k_V^*B),\quad j_U^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{U*}D,$$
$$j_V^*Rj_{V*}B\cong B,\quad j_V^*Rj_{U*}A\cong Rk_{V*}(k_U^*A),\quad j_V^*Rj_{W*}D\cong Rk_{V*}D,$$
and $Rj_{U*}Rk_{U*}\cong Rj_{W*}$, $Rj_{V*}Rk_{V*}\cong Rj_{W*}$. Here $A,B,D$ are arbitrary objects on the $U,V,W$ slices. The self-restriction identifications are the counits. For $A$ on $U$, define $r_A:Rj_{U*}A\to Rj_{W*}(k_U^*A)$ as the $j_W^*\dashv Rj_{W*}$ transpose of $k_U^*\epsilon_{U,A}$, using canonical iterated restriction; define $r_B$ likewise. The listed identifications carry $r_A|_U$ and $r_B|_V$ to the respective units for $k_U^*\dashv Rk_{U*}$ and $k_V^*\dashv Rk_{V*}$, carry $r_B|_U$ and $r_A|_V$ to the identity under the cross-identifications, and carry $r_A|_W,r_B|_W$ to identities under the self-restriction counits. All comparisons are induced on K-injective representatives by the sectionwise product identifications and preserve these adjunction maps.
